approvedDecisions: One logical operation produces one immutable event envelope containing all record changes; preserve existing bulk input partial success.
All-before becomes not_applied; all-after finalizes the saved result/event; mixed or unknown blocks only that project and requires fingerprinted explicit accept-observed.
Guarantees cover central writes and cooperating locks; external writers without common locks do not gain full atomicity.
A-04 covers existing content/milestone/config/non-secret management writes and safe password audit; continuous external/agent tracking is A-05 and review/user acceptance is A-06.
Additional user decision: guarded reads give new local paths new record keys without inventing external history events; unmatched external moves get new keys until A-05 move recognition.

scope.sqlite: Existing server.sqlite additive v4; read-only commands do not migrate.
scope.writeFlow: Current actor/access -> project queue -> guarded prepared existing Core operation -> persistent intent -> physical effects -> result/history finalize -> cache/search/WS publication.
scope.identityDiscovery: An authorized guarded read may persist a new key for a newly observed local path while the project is ready. Unmatched external moves receive a new key. This derived index update creates no content history or actor attribution; pending/recovery projects do not adopt paths.
scope.operationRead: GET /api/operations/:operationId with owner/admin and current scope access.

simplificationReview: One ServerDatabase/BEGIN IMMEDIATE policy and one transaction finalizer serve project history and management audit.
Core/FileSystem reuses existing parsers, serializer, allocator, domain handlers and locks through one prepared physical effect implementation.
One revision/snapshot implementation covers edits, lifecycle and multi-file operations; duplicate repair shares its existing preview/parser and result shape.
One operation read endpoint covers project, administration and pre-project registration with explicit scope/current-access checks.
One browser request client owns UUID/outcome handling; the existing editors and board add only conflict/recovery notices and retain their normal data paths.
Recovery uses existing boundary/inventory/MutationStore and a resolved_by link; no automatic rollback or second CRUD implementation.
limitations: Linux and isolated temporary projects only; skipped platform/PTY tests are not counted as passed.
No real project or Finbee was registered or changed; MANIFESTO.md was not edited.
Non-cooperating external writers are outside the common-lock atomicity guarantee; continuous external tracking remains A-05.
History/review/user acceptance pages and agent identity workflows remain A-05/A-06.
Raw logs, browser screenshots and temporary data under /tmp are ephemeral; this repository JSON records results, mappings and hashes, not a durable backup of those files.

The additional TSX scan retains preexisting HEAD diagnostics. Its raw exit code and baseline/current totals are recorded separately from the passing default Biome check and the zero-new-diagnostics gate.
